description: GRAPH-RESIDENT: the COST-WORTH-REFINING escalation arm, authored by the jabberwock via the composer (CLAUDE.md discipline: no hand-written agent rule) -- the OTHER half of the dual-process arbitration (the FIRST half, the ungrounded-confident arm, is seeds/composer_grounding_guard_graph.json, unmodified by this seed). Theory (creator's Graph Law review #2): the agent's cheap/fast MODEL-LAYER cognition (a basin-snap) is TRUSTED by default; it is worth abandoning for expensive ACTIVE cognition only when either (a) the snap is confidently wrong outside its grounding range (B1, composer_grounding_guard_graph's GroundingGap arm, untouched), OR (b) the snap is genuinely worth refining -- its residual*value exceeds the cost of refining it further (B2, seeds/residual_salience.json's cost_salience formula: salience(axis) = shortfall + (1-saturation) - cost; > 0 means refining pays for itself). This seed adds ONLY arm (b): mints ONE rule, escalate_cost_worth_<tag>, from an agent -wants_escalation_gate_rule-> ComposeRequest trigger (ground_concern's 'worth' relation head, seeds/relation_vocabulary.json's new cost_worth_escalate cue + seeds/composer_dispatch.json's new ComposerCue). The minted rule matches every agent -frontier_pick-> ax edge (the STANDING 'this is the cheap snap currently under consideration' signal seeds/autonomy.json's frontier-Argmax already writes -- reused, not reimplemented) where cost_salience's own per-axis value (shortfall + (1-saturation) - cost, read directly off the axis's OWN shortfall/saturation/cost attrs -- the SAME three attrs cost_salience's Argmax reads, seeds/residual_salience.json is never edited or re-evaluated as a Term here, only its formula's SHAPE is mirrored as a boolean per-axis gate) is POSITIVE and the axis has not already been cost-escalated (ax.cost_escalated is null) -- and, instead of trusting the cheap pick, mints an Impasse{kind:'cost_worth_refining'} and wires agent -surprised_by-> impasse (+ impasse -about_axis-> ax), REUSING the SAME standing surprised_by/Impasse escalation channel composer_grounding_guard_graph's arm uses (seeds/autonomy.json's mint_goal_from_surprise, already seeded, turns the surprised_by edge into a wanted Goal on its own -- this seed does not reimplement 'unexplained -> goal', it plugs a cost-worth-it verdict into that existing channel, exactly the shape the grounding-guard arm established). An axis whose cost_salience value is <= 0 (not worth refining) never gets escalated by this rule -- trust is the default; escalation is what a genuine cost/residual trade-off earns. Marks ax.cost_escalated so a re-run never re-escalates the same axis (fixpoint safety, the same guard idiom composer_grounding_guard_graph's gap.escalated flag and composer_control_graph's default_no_response use).

effect.why: the frontier pick's residual*value exceeds the cost of refining it further -- escalate to active cognition, do not trust the cheap snap
